So I'll write this review for people whom never play Warhammer 40k games before and reluctant about buying the game.

[h2]Do you need 100 Terabytes of Warhammer 40k lore injected into your brain in order to play this game?[/h2]
Short answer : Yes and No. 

Long answer : If you are a kind of guy that needs to understand the lore before playing the game or just wanted to understand the storyline in general, then there's a lot of guides out there (Youtube, Rulebooks, etc) that helps you understand the game better. [u]But remember, you'll need more time to catch them all up than actually finishing the game.[/u]

If you can just play the game without caring about the lore, well [u]you should.[/u] at least understand a little bit of it is enough. The gameplay itself is not far from Helldivers 2, except it's bigger, better, especially if you understand the lore.

In my opinion, this game is like Elden Ring. A game that made you get "into" souls-like game. And this game is what made you "into" Warhammer 40k. Because I've never interested in any Warhammer 40k before and this game successfully made me interested in Warhammer 40k universe.

[h2]How about the gameplay? Is it good?[/h2]
Hell yeah. It's good. The campaign mission is currently only about 15 hours long in low difficulty, but the devs promises future updates for more PvE mission and such. There is a lot of potential on this game that has yet to come. But there is still a lot of things to do, especially the multiplayer campaign (including PvP mode). 

The reward from such multiplayer campaign gave you "cosmetic item" of other Space Marine foundings (see, this is why you should learn the lore a bit because I don't know how to word it in other way). That is why I think only few people that really into the Warhammer that grind the game to hundred of hours to collect all "skins".

The optimization is good, I'm playing on Low-Medium on RTX 2060 and Ryzen 5 5600G and still got average 50-60 fps (depends on if you turn on background swarm on high or low). The graphics and details are beautiful, The story is good and immersive, the community is good.

[h2]You said a lot of a good things. There's literally nothing bad about it?[/h2]
There is a few, but keep in mind this is my first Warhammer game so bear that in mind.

1. Stealth installation of Epic Online Service. Yep I don't understand it, and maybe people who understand about it can explain it to you why is it a bad thing or you can do it for your quick googling research. It was ESG stealth installation or something, i don't fully understand it. You can ask the community for it.

2. I sometimes kinda get motion sickness for playing more than an hour from it even though it was never a problem in other game, but I turned off screen shakes and it stopped. Maybe it differs from person to person but me personally I hate that.

3. Ping problems for people who play in Asia region. There's also a PvP mode that I haven't played it yet, I'm in Asia and even on co-op campaign I often get high ping so I avoid PvP modes.

4. For people who don't care about cosmetics or Warhammer's lore, this game getting repetitive really fast in this current state of the game. Sure the story is amazing, but the multiplayer campaigns can be repetitive after few hours or so. The only way to avoid it is waiting until the new missions available like the devs promises. The only difference in the campaign itself is the difficulties.

5. I didn't met Henry Cavill in game.

[h2]You yap a lot for someone who's just get into Warhammer's game. Cut the chase, should I buy it?"[/h2]
If you want more hours than me and felt that it wasn't worth it to play this game just for a few hours, then wait on sale or buy it after the new PvE missions added. $60 for Warhammer fans is cheap, because being a Warhammer's fans is [u]expensive as hell,[/u]

but 60 bucks for people who don't really "into" Warhammer universe, I'd say it's pretty expensive and you could get "more hours" worth in other game with the same price. That is if you're not becoming a fan after playing the game.

or you can start from Space Marine 1 before playing this one. A lot of Warhammer fan actually prefer the SM1 rather than SM2, even though I don't know in what way.

This game has successfully turning me into a fan and changed my youtube algorhitm to Warhammer 40k, so I'd recommend this game to anyone who is into the genre of space science fiction and loves in-depth lores.

It's a great game. You'll definitely get your money's worth if you enjoy all three game modes (Campaign, PVE, PVP).

I pretty much exclusively do the Coop PVE game modes and it's very good. It's not going to be in discussions for "best horde shooter ever" and there are a lot of issues that seem small then really start to hamper enjoyment, but the dev team seems responsive to change and it's fun for at least 150 hours (which is a lot of time.)
It would be heresy to NOT recommend this game.

The graphics? Absolutely stunning! And the attention to detail is insane – like when you grapple a human enemy, pulling them right toward you instead of the other way around. It’s those little touches that make the game feel immersive. The customization for Space Marines is great, though there’s room for improvement. A bit bummed you can’t color the "fists" yet for Crimson Fists, for example.

The enemy variety is nicely mixed, and the 7 operations as side missions to the main campaign add a lot to the experience. The campaign itself? Breathtaking and totally worth it! The difficulty levels are challenging but fair – perfect for the Warhammer vibe.

The 6 classes offer variety for every playstyle. Personally, I’m all about the Tactical and Vanguard classes, but everyone will find a Space Marine to suit their style. Would’ve loved the official Games Workshop class names, but that’s just a minor gripe. And after 95 hours of playtime, I’m still not “done” with the game – now that’s value! Highly recommend it!

7.5/10 Need more polish and content for price tag, overall enjoyable once you hook the game mechanic. 

Story : A good popcorn movie which you are main heroine.
I'm not into Warhammer verse yet, I enjoy reading lore about monster and creature so I have zero interest in Space Marine side (human is boring) I also didn't plat SM1. Overall I enjoy the campaign. The design to unlock operation make sense when you play it in order and make it feel more impact to the story. Not so great, but enjoyable like good popcorn movie but you can insert yourself into.
Atmosphere is good, sound effect is very heavy and meaty satisfy. Sadly enemy look almost the same with just different weapon / slight change. Which compare to Warhammer verse it's quite a let down to have very small enemy roaster.
Campaign can be play with friend and separate completely from co-op mission progression too.

Gameplay : Downgrade modern Doom with melee addition.
As of patch 4.1 The game is not shooter unless you play specific class. Due to gun play is very basic and half of weapon belong in museum as it's damage is very very pea shooter at best.
It's basically hack and slash / muso game. You parry, doing gun strike until everything is dead. Combo is bare bone, movement is slow. You don't have much option when trading with range like Chaos faction beside simple dodge and sustain armour.
Think about modern doom, you have exact same use of glory kill in term of execution and very downgrade of that. It can be use as i-frame, positioning, recovery, bloody effect, and slow the game play. But why doom glory kill is much smoother? Better gun play allow you to swiftly kill target to target and higher mobility to re-position and dancing around battle field.

Power Fantasy : That not quite power fantasy unless you playing lower difficulty.
The power fantasy dev talk about come from super human power to sustain armour and stay healthy until the end of day. Not that you can easily rip and tear through hoard of enemy. Simply because this game also using lazy difficulty setting to add more number on enemy status. So the higher difficulty, the more spongy they are and it basic combat make it very monotonous play. Still, when you tear through each enemy one by one or more until the end of mission, you sense the satisfy of walking through enemy corpse that pile up like a mountain.

Content and Pricing : Quite overprice, end-game progression mission is too low.
While the campaign and overall mission is good, but the content is low compare to the price. Campaign exist for story and unlock co-op mission. SM2 offer replayability by having rpg-like progression in endgame co-op mission. But only 7 mission as of patch 4.1 compare to other game is quite on low end.

Overall good and solid choice if you are Warhammer fan or looking for some hack and slash. My main deduction point come from price tag, lack of polish to make it more enjoyable, content, weapon, enemy roaster, matchmaking and alike.

Have to edit this to note that the CEO of Saber Interactive (Matthew Karch) has outed himself as an absolute scumbag. As such I can't recommend supporting any game made by this developer.

I had a pretty good time with Space Marine 2. It takes everything from the first game and makes the combat more modern while keeping things relatively straightforward. Like others I found the first half more fun than the second due to the antagonists you're fighting and the second part being a bit predictable. The story isn't amazing but it's good enough. The gunplay and melee combat is fun. If you only plan to play the campaign I wouldn't recommend buying this at full price but it was an enjoyable ~8 hours for me. I hope they'll consider more single player DLC or a sequel that builds on the foundation they've established here. The biggest downside for me is the low FOV. I suffer from motion sickness and while it didn't impact me I definitely could see it impacting others so be aware of that.

It's an excellent game that met the vast majority of my expectations. I like the mechanics, I like the story, I like Saber Interactive for being so quick with patches and responses to the community. If I had a tiny gripe, it would be that their arsenal is a little bolter heavy. I would love to see some other weapons like a hand flamer, grav gun or even a combi weapon other than just the combi grenade launcher. Otherwise though the execution is spectacular, and I'm excited to see what else they have on their road map

Space Marine 2 is an incredible sequel, with a great story with a solid 8 hours of gameplay, and countless hours of fun repeatable co-op missions to grind afterwards. The customization system is awesome, being able to choose your own Chapter, pick different types of armor and weapons to slay Tyranids by the thousands. The parry system in this game feels incredible, super rewarding and you can't help but feel like a Primarch as you deal with hordes of xenos armed with only a power sword and your faith in the God-Emperor of Mankind.
